claims.statement: The code-reference verification fragment proposes a FizzBuzz completion-and-acceptance probe followed by checking the matching-code log, depending on preceding log-display instructions. Its expected common match is typical rather than deterministic; one observed match would not prove exhaustive detection, and the probe was not run.

The code-review usage fragment says agentic review capabilities, including project context collection and preview features, use Actions with hosted runners by default. Private-repository reviews consume account or organization minutes and overage is billed; exact cost and spending authorization are not supplied.

The review fragment says disabling organization-hosted runners makes agentic capabilities unavailable and yields a more limited review. A completed review alone therefore does not prove full project context or the agentic capabilities ran.

The Vim/Neovim setup fragment presents separate setup and enable commands, with configuration-file enablement as an alternative. Documentation commands are not instructions executed here or proof authenticated, enabled editor behavior.

The exclusion pattern tip describes fnmatch path notation and case-insensitive matching and links Ruby documentation. Only this source claim is reviewed; full wildcard/path/escaping semantics and actual matcher implementation remain unverified.

The exclusion limitation warns that IDE-provided indirect semantic information can still originate from excluded files, including types, symbol hover definitions and build properties. File exclusion is therefore not complete information isolation or a guarantee no derivative context is used.

The exclusion tooltip fragment describes a slashed status icon and hover text identifying the restrictive settings. This UI indicator is distinct from verified exclusion enforcement, especially given indirect semantic leakage; its screenshot asset was not visually reviewed.
